digest.component_or_area: rebar metrics command and passive instrumentation
propositions: Rebar lacks an aggregation layer and cannot derive agent-loop trends over time despite having a rich event-sourced history of tickets, gates, code health, and git events.

Three tier-C blindspots leave no durable trace in the event store: env/integration-diagnosis intervals, bug provenance (which prior change caused this bug), and bug outcome classification (regression vs plan-defect vs flaky).

A single `rebar metrics` command with date-range filtering must surface every available metric across agent-loop health, codebase decay, and gate economics, with structured unavailable states for metrics without yet-accrued signals.

Passive instrumentation must close blindspots via trustworthy code (gate error handlers, git blame) rather than agent self-report: ERROR outcomes on gate sidecars for diagnosis intervals, best-effort blame-derived caused_by links for bug provenance, and persisted close_class enum (replacing free-text reason) for bug classification.
Bug-close friction must remain flat: the required free-text reason is replaced by a bounded enum persisted on the STATUS event, with no net increase in required arguments.

All backfilled/classified metrics must be labeled source=backfill_classified and confidence=classified so they never feed authoritative structural series and remain segregated from trustworthy structural derivation.
